subject: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots

Team —

Quick context: EchoHealth is kicking off a low-latency pilot (demo late Nov) that needs a small, temporary slice of dedicated capacity to hit sub-150ms p95 on 1k qps-ish bursts. They asked for a "hotlane" style reservation for 72 hours during their internal load tests. Before I commit anything, I want product/ops/legal alignment on how we gate access and what we require in return (SLA exceptions, committed spend, telemetry hooks).

Key asks:
- Confirm criteria for granting hotlane access (product): what metrics/commitments must the pilot meet?
- Ops: what is the minimum runway and how do we isolate without impacting other reserved pools?
- Finance/Legal: what approvals/documentation do we need if we offer credits or short-term carveouts?

Attached are a draft criteria doc and a simple reservation matrix I started. Please review and flag any hard no's. If we can align today, I'll present a short summary to EchoHealth this afternoon.

Attachments: hotlane_criteria_draft.pdf, pilot_reservation_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots

Thanks Priya — good framing. A few product concerns / proposed modifications:

1) Criteria: let's require at minimum:
   - defined p95 target and test harness (doc link okay)
   - reproducible load script + expected token mix
   - agreement to run tests during a 72-hour window with telemetry enabled (trace + token-level cost reporting)

2) Isolation: we should avoid full GPU carveouts unless absolutely necessary. Prefer:
   - temporary top-priority routing to a small standby pool (up to 2 GPUs for small pilots) OR
   - burst buffer with explicit soft-fallback to hosted variants if capacity constrained

3) Term: limit to a single 72-hour window per pilot; additional windows require product approval + ops signoff.

I think the pilot_reservation_matrix.xlsx should include expected qps/avg seq len/expected token-hour estimate — Marcus can you confirm what we need to provision?

If we can capture the above, I can sign off product-side.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots

On Nov 1, 2026, at 11:05 AM, Kimberly Park wrote:
> I think the pilot_reservation_matrix.xlsx should include expected qps/avg seq len/expected token-hour estimate — Marcus can you confirm what we need to provision?

Short answers + ops constraints:

- Minimum practical carveout: 1 x A100-equivalent slot for very small, warm models; 2 slots to support warm + burst headroom. Anything less and latency SLOs are brittle.
- Autoscale exceptions: we can allow an exception to normal autoscale (i.e., reserve fixed capacity) but only with:
   * explicit time window (start/end)
   * canary fallback route that drops to compatible quantized variant if we exhaust reservation
   * circuit-breaker thresholds tied to cluster-wide utilization (we won't starve existing reserved customers)

Cost/ops trade-offs: provisioning 2 slots for 72 hours is roughly X token-hours cost (see matrix). If product insists on larger carveouts, we need finance approval for potential overage credits.

Practical ops asks: populate pilot_reservation_matrix with: expected peak qps, p95 latency target, model name + size, avg sequence length, warmup strategy, and whether KV-cache will be preloaded. That will let us calculate exact GPU-hours and whether we need memory-optimized machines.

I opened JIRA INF-7823 to track the exception work and added a short checklist. Linking it here: JIRA: INF-7823.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots

Couple of procurement/legal notes:

- If EchoHealth requests credits or a formal short-term SLA, Finance needs a one-paragraph justification and expected $ impact (noted in the matrix). Please include how this pilot ties to renewal/expansion (commercial rationale).
- For exceptions to autoscale that could affect SLAs for other customers, we need an exec-level approval route. I can draft an email template for the Biz Ops lead if you want.
- Attachment checklist: we should collect an SOC2 evidence pointer if they plan any workload-modifying testing; at minimum require security contact and test schedule.

Once Marcus gives the provisioning calc, I can run numbers and advise whether credits are acceptable or if we should require a minimum prepaid reservation.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Commercial Operations (Finance & Legal Liaison)

Subject: Re: Temporary high-priority access criteria & reservation policy for low-latency pilots

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick plan of record:

1) Product (Kimberly): finalize criteria doc with p95 target, required load script, and the single-window policy. I'll attach the final doc to the pilot ticket.
2) Ops (Marcus): run numbers based on the matrix (I'll update with EchoHealth's expected avg seq length today). Target carveout: 2-slot hotlane for a 72-hour window with a canary fallback route.
3) Finance/Legal (Dev): please propose either a small prepaid reservation or up-to-X credits; I'll include the commercial rationale in the one-paragraph note for approval.

Action: I'm scheduling a 30-min sync tomorrow 11:00am PT to walk through the reservation matrix and sign off (calendar invite to follow). If anyone has a hard no on the 2-slot approach, raise it in the next 12 hours so I can adjust before the invite.
